# A scene worth entering

Use this small card for a new story, comic or game scene. Fill it in once, then
make the scene. Keep deeper research in linked records rather than in the dialogue.
Existing scientific freezes and source terms still apply.

**Place and season:** Which part of the basin? What makes it recognizable?

**Person and immediate want:** What do they need today, beyond understanding a system?

**One spatial invention:** What changes a route, room, boundary or ordinary action?
What is worn, missing, awkward or unavailable?

**Encounter and choice:** Who else wants something? Give the person a choice with a
small consequence. Keep room for humor, pleasure, leisure and a life after work.

**Three image beats:** An establishing view; hands doing something; the consequence.
Use a distinct camera for each. A comic can make these panels; a game can make
them locations or interactions.

**Grounding, briefly:** Link one or two useful existing records. State what is
observed, conditional and invented. Invented devices need no fake performance number.

**Reusable hook:** Which person, object, place or unfinished question could return?

Finish when someone can read, see or play it. For a reversible creative prototype,
check continuity, legibility, choices and links once; don’t create a new phase of
review paperwork. A claim about the real world needs its own appropriate evidence.

Example: [Before the Last Bus](../../stories/before_the_last_bus.md),
[Reading Hall visual workshop](../../reports/creative_development_2026-10-03.md).
